english_title: Lemma in the Fourier Transform Version
statement_en: If $f \in L^1(\mathbb{R}^n)$, and its Fourier transform is defined by $$\hat{f}(\xi) = \int_{\mathbb{R}^n}f(x)e^{-2\pi i x \cdot \xi } \, dx,$$ then $$|\hat{f}(\xi)|\to 0 \text{ as } |\xi| \to \infty.$$ Since the Fourier transform of an integrable function is continuous, this is essentially the statement that $$f \in L^1(\mathbb{R}^n) \implies \hat{f} \in C_0(\mathbb{R}^n).$$
final_code:
import Mathlib

open MeasureTheory Real Complex Topology Filter

theorem integrable_fourier_transform_vanishes_at_infinity
    {n : ℕ} (f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℂ) (hf : Integrable f) :
    ∃ fhat : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℂ,
      (∀ ξ, fhat ξ = ∫ x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), f x * Complex.exp (-(2 * Real.pi * Complex.I) * ((∑ i : Fin n, x i * ξ i) : ℂ)) ∂volume) ∧
      Continuous fhat ∧
      ∀ u : ℕ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n),
        Tendsto (fun m => ‖u m‖) atTop atTop →
        Tendsto (fun m => ‖fhat (u m)‖) atTop (nhds 0) := by
  sorry
